Hi Sara / Raj -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from my side:

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary concern: noisy-neighbor interference on shared (hosted) pools - you need consistent p95 latency and no cross-tenant tail latency spikes.
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 generation latency < 250ms, sustained throughput ~150 req/s for peak windows.
- Data residency: US-East for both inference and logging.
- Timeline: procurement + SOC review in March, PoC in April if possible.

Options we discussed:
1) Hosted API - fastest to start, cost-efficient, but shared pools may see noisy-neighbor interference under high bursty workloads. Good fit for non-latency-critical workloads.
2) Dedicated capacity - reserved GPU pools (pinned capacity) with allocation isolation; recommended when you need predictable latency and isolation.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) - for strict compliance/data residency; more setup time but complete isolation.

Follow-ups I can do this week:
- Share our dedicated offering flyer and a draft SLA (attached).
- Put Priyom (infra) and Marissa (deploy) on a thread for a technical deep-dive on isolation options and SLO guarantees.
- Propose a short PoC scope and timeline.

Questions for you to help us size the PoC:
- Typical request size / model family you plan to use? (e.g., 2k token completions vs chat embeddings)
- Expected peak QPS in your peak 15-minute window?
- Any internal SRE/ops people you want on the PoC calls?

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-flyer.pdf, SLA-draft-FT-042.docx

Next step: can we lock a 60-min technical deep-dive next week (week of Mar 1)? I'll include Priyom and Marissa for isolation/SLO specifics.

Great questions - looping Priyom and Marissa on the SLO/isolation specifics. Short answers while they chime in:

- Dedicated pools: you get reserved GPU capacity and process isolation at the scheduler level. We can pin capacity to a customer pool and configure autoscale policies with reserved baseline + burst buffer. That means your baseline throughput (e.g., 150 req/s) is guaranteed, and bursts can consume additional capacity if unused in the fleet subject to configured burst limits.
- Noisy-neighbor mitigations we commonly use: pinned capacity, strict scheduler QoS for tenant processes, per-tenant KV cache partitions, and per-tenant token rate limits.
- SLA/SLO: happy to share our standard SLO language - see attached draft. We can add remediation clauses for latency regressions tied to noisy neighbor events (credits / escalation windows).

Priyom/Marissa - can you confirm suggested p95/p99 targets and what we'd propose for the PoC (profile-based capacity sizing + 2-week load window)? Also please attach any internal runbook snippets (network isolation, tenancy model) that help procurement/SRE review.

Thanks - added a few proposed SLOs and isolation mitigations below (and attached the PDF with details):

Proposed SLOs (for discussion):
- p95 generation latency: <= 250ms (measured at API gateway egress)
- p99 generation latency: <= 800ms (initially; can be tightened post-PoC)
- availability: 99.9% monthly for dedicated pools
- incident remediation: acknowledge within 1 hour, mitigation plan within 4 hours for latency regressions caused by infra events

Isolation / noisy-neighbor mitigations:
- Pinned GPU capacity: dedicate N GPUs to the customer pool for baseline throughput.
- Scheduler QoS: tenant-level cgroups and process priorities to prevent CPU/GPU preemption.
- Per-tenant KV cache partitioning: avoids cross-tenant evictions impacting cache hit rates.
- Network QoS & VPC peering: isolate control plane and customer VPC egress to reduce noisy network interference.
- Audit + tracing: per-tenant traces so we can attribute tail-latency spikes to a root cause.

PoC proposal (high level):
Week 0: onboarding & model selection + baseline profiling (collect token distribution, latency heatmaps)
Week 1-2: dedicated pool run with synthetic and replayed traffic (validate p95/p99 and stability)
Week 3: stabilization & configuration tuning, deliver final report and recommended committed capacity

Next step: I recommend we schedule the technical deep-dive with FintechCo engineers next Wed (Mar 3) - I'll bring the PoC sketch and a sizing table. Sara/Raj - which time window works for you (10-12 PT or 2-4 PT)?
